transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

For the past three weeks, my mind has felt constantly foggy and I just can't seem to focus on anything. I also feel completely emotionally numb, like my head is totally empty. I decided to come in because I'm really struggling to get through the day like this.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful or traumatic event happened to you? If so, what happened?

Yes, they started about three weeks ago after a really stressful and traumatic event. But I honestly don't want to talk about what happened or describe it. Just thinking about it is incredibly painful, and I'm trying as hard as I can to avoid those memories.
Have these symptoms been present for less than one month since the traumatic event, or have they lasted longer than a month?
It has been about three weeks since everything started. So yes, it has been less than a month.
Since the event, have you been having things like unwanted memories or nightmares, feeling on edge, or feeling detached or unreal?

I do feel incredibly detached and emotionally numb, as if my mind is completely empty of any feelings. I am actively trying my best to avoid any thoughts or memories associated with the event, but I haven't really had nightmares or felt particularly on edge.
Since this happened, have there been times when the world feels unreal, you feel outside your body, or you cannot remember important parts of what happened?

No, I haven't felt like the world is unreal or like I'm outside of my body, and I remember the event clearly. My mind does feel very foggy, though, and I keep forgetting small everyday things like where I put my keys. But I haven't experienced those other feelings.
Even if you try to avoid thinking about it, do upsetting memories of the event ever pop into your mind on their own or feel like you are reliving it?
I try very hard to avoid thinking about the event altogether. Because of that, I don't really have upsetting memories suddenly popping into my mind, and I've never felt like I was reliving it.
Since the event, have you been more irritable, had trouble sleeping, been unusually jumpy, or found it hard to concentrate?

I have been having a really difficult time concentrating, like struggling to focus on reading, watching TV, or keeping up with conversations. However, I haven't really experienced those other issues like irritability, sleep problems, or feeling jumpy.
Are these symptoms causing major problems in your work, school, relationships, or daily functioning beyond what you would expect from the stress itself?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. My mind has been so foggy lately that I haven't been able to think clearly about how it's impacting my work or relationships.
Can you give me one concrete example of how this has affected your day-to-day functioning, like at work, school, home, or in relationships?

Lately, I struggle with simple daily decisions, like taking forever just to choose what to wear or eat in the morning. I also constantly lose focus during conversations and keep forgetting where I put everyday items like my keys. Even basic, routine tasks feel overwhelming because my mind is so foggy.
Since the event, have you also had a very low mood, felt unable to experience positive emotions, or made strong efforts to avoid places, people, or situations that remind you of it?

Yes, I actively avoid any places, people, or conversations that remind me of the event because it is just too painful. I also feel completely emotionally numb, unable to experience any happiness, joy, or even love and affection toward my family. It feels like all of my positive emotions are entirely blocked.
